notes.text: Historical editorial lesson: HungryCrab digesting repository material and desktop-fly moving articulated legs do not establish automatic bug detection. A proposed prototype must name the mapping from a digest field to a motor or visual behavior.

Historical editorial lesson: mapping logic flows to joint movements is too vague without a named input field and an explicit mapping rule. Keep a proposed adapter visibly separate from either donor's existing capabilities.
Historical editorial lesson: edition-linked literary measurements are not evidence of sentiment analysis. Use only the narrower purpose supported by the actual Scriptorium excerpt.

Historical editorial lesson: a kinship source register organizes artifacts and claims; it does not automatically prove identity or family relationships. A useful proposal can create a queue for human archival review.

Historical editorial lesson: carry the same donor-specific collision through hook, curse and first words. A random prop or job can be funny while providing weak recognizable inheritance. Fictional inconvenience is not a diagnosis of a real repository.

Historical editorial lesson: a schema-valid card with valid evidence IDs can still overstate a technical bridge. A second model's review is an interpretation and cannot certify that the proposed prototype is feasible.
